Description: In the Kitchen, John Hobbes and Edmund Galley handle the second body and have a direct conversation, making the first explicit accusations and suspicions around the servant’s death, Rupert Galley’s identity, and potential suspects.
Location: Kitchen (Kitchen)
Key Information:
  - John Hobbes and Edmund Galley work together in the Kitchen to move a heavy body, confirming this is the second deceased person found in the villa.
  - The deceased carries a pantry key; Edmund Galley uses this to judge the person is the servant responsible for preparing dinner.
  - The servant’s specific identity has not yet been officially confirmed.
  - Based on existing role assignments and the timeline: Person No. 11 Harry Thornton has been active as the butler in earlier nodes and is highly associated with the Kitchen and logistics. Therefore, the deceased servant is suspected to be Person No. 11 Harry Thornton, but this is only speculation and has not been verified.
  - Edmund Galley admits he is not familiar with household servant matters, which are usually handled by Martha Galley.
  - Edmund Galley directly questions John Hobbes about his purpose for visiting, Rupert Galley’s identity, and the link between the two deaths.
  - John Hobbes reiterates he does not know Rupert Galley, only confirms he is the invitation signatory, and says he “instinctively” recognized him upon seeing the body.
  - Edmund Galley explicitly states the two deaths cannot be treated as a coincidence and demands John Hobbes promise not to affect the other guests further.
  - John Hobbes points out that during dinner time he stayed with others in the Dining room; if there was deliberate intent, it is more likely to come from someone inside the villa.
  - Edmund Galley notes that two people were absent during dinner; one is ruled out as a suspect, and the other is Oswald.
  - Edmund Galley reveals Oswald’s family relationship for the first time: he has appeared since childhood as an “uncle,” but his biological father is unknown.
  - Based on this, John Hobbes judges Oswald may know Rupert Galley, making him the most important lead.
  - Edmund Galley believes Oswald may go to the Dining room to eat after everyone leaves and instructs John Hobbes to go to the Dining room to find him.
  - After John Hobbes leaves the Kitchen, Edmund Galley stays behind alone; the sound of liquid being poured is heard, then Edmund Galley leaves the Kitchen.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · Helps move the second body.
    · Again denies any connection to Rupert Galley or the two deaths.
    · Proposes Oswald may be the key breakthrough.
    · Accepts Edmund Galley’s instruction and goes to the Dining room to find Oswald.
  [Edmund Galley (Edmund Galley)] Person No. 6, one of the villa’s hosts.
    · Identifies the deceased as the servant responsible for preparing dinner.
    · Directly questions and warns John Hobbes.
    · Explains Oswald’s complicated relationship to his family for the first time.
    · Stays alone in the Kitchen after John Hobbes leaves and performs unknown liquid handling.
  [Harry Thornton (Thornton)] Person No. 11, suspected to be the logistics servant.
    · The deceased is judged to be the servant responsible for preparing dinner.
    · Based on duties and earlier Kitchen-related activity records, the deceased’s identity is speculated to be Person No. 11 Harry Thornton.
    · Formal identity confirmation has not been completed; it can only be treated as suspected.
  [Oswald (Oswald)] A key person mentioned, Edmund Galley’s nominal “uncle.”
    · Is absent during dinner.
    · Is suspected of possibly knowing Rupert Galley.
    · Is believed to potentially go to the Dining room after everyone leaves.
